niche.habitat: Upper troposphere (2–5 km), within ring-shadow bands and magnetic valleys. Also, in the council's sketch (no such creature in this world yet): Polvo-Vivo, anillo-Sangre is the apex predator of the ring-rain filter-feeder community; Polvo-Vivo graze on the same dust but cannot harvest static charge, making them easy prey for the Anillo-Sangre's arc
niche.diet: Electro-autotrophy (static charge harvest), chemosynthetic CO₂ fixation, particulate ring-dust
niche.active: Continuous, but peaks during atmospheric tide shear and eclipse thermal contraction

body: Biradial, flexible, filamentous body of piezoelectric silicate and conductive melanin-carotenoid matrix; lacks rigid skeleton, relies on turgor pressure and magnetic alignment

chains.trait: Piezoelectric filaments harvest tidal strain as metabolic voltage
links: Silicate crystal fibers generate voltage under mechanical stress
ATP synthesis driven by harvest current

skill.effect: When wind gusts or the player pull and stretch its body, the creature moves swiftly and quickly recovers its energy.

chains.weakness: Rigidity: Coating in resin or freezing immobilizes filaments, cutting power source and halting regeneration
observe: Filaments pulsing in rhythm with the giant's gravitational pull
Faint glow emanating from cracks in the body when bent
Moves faster and more erratically during high wind shear

plausibility.summary: Power the filaments from F11 atmospheric-tide wind shear and gust flex (player stretch = same physics), with piezo/tribo as a boost layer; keep chemosynthetic CO₂ fixation and ring-dust as the main carbon/energy budget; treat the 58 h giant cycle as a behavioral sync cue (movement pulses), not literal orbital stretch eating.
fixes: Power the filaments from F11 atmospheric-tide wind shear and gust flex (player stretch = same physics), with piezo/tribo as a boost layer; keep chemosynthetic CO₂ fixation and ring-dust as the main carbon/energy budget; treat the 58 h giant cycle as a behavioral sync cue (movement pulses), not literal orbital stretch eating.

analogues.organism: Piezoelectricity in mineralized tissues (e.g. bone under load); acetogens and related microbes that couple extracellular electrons to carbon fixation on cathodes—not piezo filaments.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Triboelectric fronds generate lethal electrostatic discharge
links: Permanent atmospheric tides drive high wind shear
Friction charges filaments against insulating cuticle
Arc discharges at threshold to stun prey and deter predators

skill.effect: After gathering energy, the creature lashes out with an electric whip that briefly stuns nearby targets, draining its stored power.

chains.weakness: Grounding: Standing in conductive mud or water shorts the cuticle, instantly draining charge and paralyzing the creature
observe: Sparks jumping between fronds before an attack
Prey frozen mid-leap with fur/hair standing on end
Sings a crackling hum as charge builds to threshold

journal.en: The sky's lightning, bottled and angry.

plausibility.summary: Frame Arc-Whip as a high-voltage stun/corona poke on small prey and rivals, not cloud-to-ground lightning; require charge buildup in dry ring-shadow/shear zones; weakness to mud/water grounding stays honest. Optionally note facultative feeding on fair-weather atmospheric electricity as garnish, not sole diet.
fixes: Frame Arc-Whip as a high-voltage stun/corona poke on small prey and rivals, not cloud-to-ground lightning; require charge buildup in dry ring-shadow/shear zones; weakness to mud/water grounding stays honest. analogues.organism: Electric eel (Electrophorus) — high-voltage offensive organs via electrocytes; spiders and insects that accumulate and use environmental static (e.g. electrostatic-assisted silk ballooning and prey interaction).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Ring ice and dust scatter incident starlight
Scattering produces highly polarized sky background
Ommatidia detect e-vector angle for precise compass

skill.effect: Reveals hidden paths, enemies, or resources through heavy haze, fog, or during the 40-minute eclipse when visual landmarks vanish

chains.weakness: Glare: Intense direct stellar flare or unfiltered starlight washes out polarization contrast, causing temporary blindness
observe: Eyes rotating independently to sample different polarization planes
Tracks the shimmering dust of falling ring particles
Maintains straight flight through total darkness using sky polarization

journal.en: It reads the compass of the rings.

plausibility.summary: F18’s stable polarized skylight is exactly the cue animals use when the sun is obscured or haze blocks landmarks; independent eye rotation to sample e-vector angles matches known ommatidial designs. During F12’s 40 min eclipse, twilight-level ring-scattered light can still carry polarization if the rings remain in view—navigation in heavy haze/eclipse is well within arthropod-grade solutions at 0.83 g.
fixes: F18’s stable polarized skylight is exactly the cue animals use when the sun is obscured or haze blocks landmarks; independent eye rotation to sample e-vector angles matches known ommatidial designs. analogues.organism: Honey bee and desert ant sky-compass polarization vision; dung beetle orientation when the sun is not visible.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Magnetotactic migration to induced magnetic valleys
links: Induced magnetosphere creates localized magnetic valleys
Conductive blood and filaments align with magnetic flux
Creature steers along field lines to reach low-radiation zones

skill.effect: The creature senses and reveals hidden magnetic valleys, allowing the player to direct it toward these sheltered areas for protection.

chains.weakness: Magnetic Dead Zones: In regions of null field, the creature loses navigation, panics, and drifts randomly, becoming vulnerable
observe: Spins slowly to sample magnetic direction before moving
Dives into shadowed pockets where radiation instruments drop
Body aligns perfectly with invisible field lines like iron filings

journal.en: It feels the giant's invisible grip.

plausibility.summary: Treat Flux-Sense as magnetoreception plus radiation-avoidance (symbiont stress pigments, UV/rad damage cues) steering toward F7 shielded pockets; require magnetite or similar inclusions in the conductive matrix for alignment aesthetics; soften null-field panic to disorientation unless multiple cues fail. Russo (2012) is electrotaxis (electric fields), not a substitute for magnetic navigation—cite only if you add galvanotaxis toward charge gradients near vents.

analogues.organism: Magnetotactic bacteria (magnetite chains); long-distance magnetoreception in sea turtles and migratory birds—gradient/map sense rather than simple dipole alignment.

body_plan.origin: Tidal flexing selected for continuous flexible filament growth to maximize surface-to-volume ratio for triboelectric harvest and strain-energy conversion

temperament: Solitary, territorial over high-charge updrafts; docile when fully charged, aggressive discharge when depleted
secrets: The piezoelectric crystals in Anillo-Sangre's filaments can be harvested by the player to craft a weak 'Strain-Cell' power source, but only if the creature is captured at peak tension (after a wind shear event).

Carrying a strong magnet near the Anillo-Sangre causes it to attempt to feed on the magnetic field; the creature becomes docile and follows the player, but its discharge ability is suppressed while magnetically loaded.

Anillo-Sangre spores are highly conductive; scattering them in water creates a conductive zone that can be used by the player to trigger environmental electrical puzzles, but will short out player electronics if the zone is too large.
moments: During the 40-minute eclipse, the Anillo-Sangre detaches a long conductive filament, impaling it onto a raised silicate spire to draw down the gas giant's accumulated charge. The creature glows like a dying star, veins of light racing through its body as it reabsorbs the lightning, then retracts the filament with a sound like tearing silk.

journal.en: It bleeds light to keep its heart beating.
